features.title: Capture text clips
features.summary: Every text copy becomes a history entry with a short preview and the full body.

features.title: Capture image clips
features.summary: Images are stored with a thumbnail and served to the webview through a custom media URI scheme.

features.title: Capture copied file lists
features.summary: Explorer copies are decoded from the DROPFILES clipboard format and each path is listed in the detail pane.

features.title: Respect clipboard opt-out flags
features.summary: Copies marked with ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing, or with history or cloud upload disabled, are never captured.

features.title: Summon the overlay with a global hotkey
features.summary: Alt+V by default, configurable in settings with validation before the shortcut is registered.

features.title: Tray menu and background operation
features.summary: Tray icon toggles the overlay and exposes open, clear unpinned history, settings and quit.

features.title: Enforce a single running instance
features.summary: Launching again raises the running window instead of adding a second tray icon and hotkey.

features.title: Closing hides instead of quitting
features.summary: The close button and Alt+F4 hide the window so the clipboard watcher keeps running; quitting stays in the tray menu.

features.title: Launch at login
features.summary: Optional startup registration that brings the watcher back after a reboot, still hidden.

features.title: Optionally hide when focus is lost
features.summary: Off by default so the window behaves as an inspection surface; the overlay behaviour is opt-in.

features.title: Ranked search as you type
features.summary: Results rank by exact match, word boundaries, position and recency over an in-memory decrypted index.

features.title: De-duplicate clips and promote reuse
features.summary: Copying the same payload promotes the existing entry and the reused clip jumps back to the top.

features.title: Pin, collect and tag clips
features.summary: Pinned clips survive bulk clears, and collections plus tags group history without duplicating it.

features.title: Retention pruning and clear history
features.summary: Old clips are pruned by policy, and clearing history can keep pinned entries.

features.title: Preview text, images and file paths
features.summary: The detail pane shows the full text, the image, or every path before the clip is reused.

features.title: List and card layouts with interface scaling
features.summary: Rows for reading text, cards for browsing images, adjustable card size and a 70-200% text scale using CSS zoom.

features.title: Collapsible preview pane
features.summary: The detail pane collapses from its top-left chevron, giving the list or grid the full width.

features.title: Opt-in paste back into the foreground app
features.summary: Scope 2 pastes into the window that had focus before the overlay opened, using scan codes so raw-input apps work too.

features.title: Encrypt clip payloads at rest
features.summary: A DPAPI-wrapped data key seals preview, body and file columns with AES-256-GCM under a fresh nonce per record.

features.title: Per-user NSIS installer
features.summary: No elevation prompt, an Apps & features entry, and app data kept outside the install directory.

features.title: Setting page dynamic search
features.summary: A search box at the top of the settings page narrows the page as you type; name matches rank above description matches, and a matching section heading keeps all of its rows.

features.title: Draggable card-size slider
features.summary: The tile view's -/+ zoom buttons are replaced by a draggable slider that applies the card size when the drag ends.

features.title: Configurable clip storage location
features.summary: The data folder can be chosen in settings; moving it copies the database, media and key, restarts, and removes the old copy.

features.title: Gear-style settings icon
features.summary: The sun-like title bar glyph was replaced with a proper gear outline.

features.title: Themes with color pickers
features.summary: Dark and light presets plus a custom mode with a swatch and hex field per color token; palettes are applied as CSS custom properties.

features.title: Collection hover actions no longer overlap the count
features.summary: The clip count hides while a collection's hover actions are shown, so archive and delete no longer sit on top of it.

features.title: Archive collections
features.summary: Collections can be archived: their clips leave the history views and search, survive clear-history and retention, and return when unarchived.

features.title: Retention by hours or days
features.summary: The maximum age can be expressed in hours or days, and archived clips are exempt from every retention limit.

features.title: Copy button in list and card views
features.summary: Hovering a row or card reveals a copy button that copies without hiding the window, unlike Enter or double click.

features.title: Search covers tag names
features.summary: Tag names are folded into the in-memory search index, so a clip filed under #invoice turns up for "invoice" even when its body never says the word.

features.title: Confirmation before deleting a collection
features.summary: Deleting a collection opens a confirmation dialog that spells out that the clips themselves are kept.

features.title: Order by dropdown in the history views
features.summary: The toolbar offers last-used or capture-date ordering in either direction; pinned clips stay on top and search relevance still wins while typing.

features.title: Remove the Enter-copies hint from the status bar
features.summary: The bottom bar no longer claims what Enter does; it keeps the clip count, storage use, encryption state and hotkey.

features.title: Searchable text in screenshots
features.summary: Images are read in the background with the built-in Windows OCR engine and the recognised text is encrypted, indexed for search, shown in the detail pane, and copyable from a hover button on the card.

features.title: Settings toggles stay inside their pill when zoomed
features.summary: The switch knob is centred with flexbox and clipped by the track, so fractional rounding at non-100% interface scales can no longer push it outside.

features.title: Auto-update from GitHub releases
features.summary: A signed in-place updater checks the latest GitHub release once a day (toggleable in settings), shows an install banner, downloads with progress and relaunches; a tag-triggered workflow builds and publishes the signed artefacts.

features.title: Card size resizes live while dragging
features.summary: The grid follows a local scale while the slider moves and the setting is written after the gesture pauses, so thumbnails resize under the pointer.

features.title: Per-category default view
features.summary: Every history category keeps its own list/cards choice, configurable in Appearance; images default to cards and everything else to rows.

features.title: Reveal clips and archives in Explorer
features.summary: Right-clicking a clip reveals its stored image or original file/folder; right-clicking an archive opens its dedicated folder under archives/, which follows renames and disappears when empty.

features.title: Always on Top setting preference
features.summary: Settings → Window → Always on top keeps the overlay above other applications; off by default and applied at startup as well as immediately when toggled.

features.title: Recognise color codes as swatches
features.summary: A payload that is entirely a hex or rgb()/rgba() value is recognised as a color: cards, rows and the preview pane paint the sample with the copied code overlaid, and a dedicated Colors view lists them.

features.title: Pause capture with a private mode
features.summary: A tray menu, a second global hotkey and a settings row pause clipboard capture for 15 minutes, an hour, or until restart; the watcher ignores changes while paused and the status bar shows a resume chip.

features.title: Quick-paste slots with Ctrl+1-9
features.summary: Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+9 copy the matching visible result without moving the selection, auto-pasting when that setting is on; rows and cards show their slot number.

features.title: Auto-clear the clipboard after use
features.summary: Optionally empties the Windows clipboard a configurable time after a copy, or as soon as the overlay hides, and leaves it alone if anything else was copied in the meantime.

features.title: Manage tags from the sidebar
features.summary: A right-click menu on a tag renames it, merges it into an existing tag, paints it with a color shown in the sidebar, or deletes it from every clip, and the search index is refreshed either way.

features.title: Save clips to disk
features.summary: Save as... writes a clip into a folder of your choosing: the stored PNG for images, copies of the original files for file lists, and the text (plus an HTML copy when present) for text clips, with unique names.

features.title: Include archived clips in search
features.summary: An Archives toggle in the search bar and an in:archive operator let a query reach clips filed in archive collections, which stay hidden from ordinary searches.

features.title: Multi-select with bulk actions
features.summary: Ctrl/Shift-click and Ctrl+A pick several clips, and a bulk bar pins, tags, files into a collection, or deletes the whole selection through new backend bulk commands.

features.title: Search operators and saved searches
features.summary: kind:, type:, app:, tag:, collection:, before:, pinned:, color: and in:archive are parsed from the search box and shown as removable chips; any query can be saved to the sidebar as a smart view.

features.title: Content-aware actions for recognised clips
features.summary: Color recognition now also classifies links, email addresses, Windows paths and JSON, and the preview pane and context menu offer matching actions: open a link, open or reveal a path, pretty-print JSON.

features.title: Drag clips into other applications
features.summary: Rows and cards can be dragged out of the overlay: text travels as text/plain, images and file lists as text/uri-list, with the payload pre-loaded on hover so the drop lands immediately.

features.title: Rich-text capture and paste as plain text
features.summary: CF_HTML and RTF are captured next to the plain body, stored encrypted in their own columns, and written back on copy so a styled clip pastes styled; a setting turns it off to paste plain text only.

features.title: Tag Filter
features.summary: A filter box under the Tags heading narrows the sidebar tag list as you type; Enter jumps to the first match and Esc clears it.

features.title: Utilities section with an emoji browser
features.summary: A new Utilities sidebar section opens a searchable emoji browser: click copies an emoji, right-click adds it to Favourites (shown first) or removes it from Favourites while leaving it in the library.

features.title: Bulk collect with a new collection name
features.summary: Typing a new collection name in the bulk Collect prompt creates the collection and files the selection into it, instead of sending a null collection id that the backend rejected.

features.title: Properties sidebar in card view
features.summary: The preview pane is shown in both layouts, so tags, collections, the archive slot and the full preview are reachable without switching to the list.

features.title: Resizable properties sidebar
features.summary: The pane's left edge is a drag handle: width is clamped to a usable 200 px minimum and 80% of the window, and the chosen width is stored in the settings.

features.title: Recognise bare hex and CSS Color 4 rgb()

features.title: Export multiple selected items

features.title: Collections and archives are separate areas

Emoji glyphs are also warmed into Chromium's glyph cache while the view is idle, which removes the one-to-two-frame stalls when new rows scroll into view without shipping any raster assets.

features.title: Flag likely API keys and secrets
features.summary: Detect secrets in text at capture time and mark the clip. High-precision rules cover PEM private keys, known token prefixes (GitHub ghp_/github_pat_, Stripe sk_live_, Slack xox*, Google AIza, OpenAI sk-proj-, Anthropic sk-ant-, npm, SendGrid, Twilio, AWS AKIA/ASIA), JWTs, URLs with embedded credentials and authorization headers. An opt-in heuristic adds Shannon entropy plus keyword context (password, api_key, client_secret) and stays off by default. Detection runs on plaintext in read_content before encryption and persists only a confidence level in the plaintext bookkeeping columns, so list rendering never decrypts. Previews are blurred with click-to-reveal, and a separate setting can skip capture entirely. Passwords are deliberately out of scope for text matching because they are indistinguishable from product codes, so they stay covered by clipboard opt-out formats and the ignored-apps list. Detection stays fully local and no match details are ever logged.

features.title: Capture the full animated GIF when a GIF is copied from a browser
features.summary: Windows has no animated-GIF clipboard format, so a browser's Copy image only ever supplies the frame it is showing. Capture now inspects the CF_HTML fragment that rides along with an image copy for an / GIF (including small data: URLs) and fetches the source asset off the watcher thread. The downloaded animation is stored as .gif beside the still frame, which remains the thumbnail and OCR source. The clip is marked animated, so copy/paste republishes the file through CF_HDROP instead of a bitmap and every frame survives in chat apps and editors. The path is not limited to GIPHY and never touches the GIPHY key or its rate limits. Because arbitrary hosts are allowed it uses a general HTTPS-only fetcher: it resolves and rejects loopback, private, link-local and CGNAT addresses, refuses credentials and non-standard ports, pins redirects to the original host, requires an image/gif content type, keeps the 32 MB cap and request timeout, and sniffs the GIF header before caching. Edge cases: CF_HDROP wins, so copying a real .gif in Explorer already yields the full animation. blob: URLs are skipped, hotlink failures and non-GIF responses fall back silently to the static frame at debug level, and inline data: GIFs are decoded up to a 2 MB ceiling.

features.title: Add expand/collapse functionality to text menu item

features.title: add zoomed color view to the cursor when selecting a color with eyedropper
features.summary: The screen sampler now shows a small topmost magnifier beside the crosshair from the moment the pick starts. It displays a 15×15 pixel zoom of the area under the cursor, outlines the exact pixel the click will read, and names the colour as both hex and rgb in a footer chip. The popup follows the cursor across the virtual desktop, flips at monitor edges, never takes focus or intercepts clicks, and disappears when the pick finishes or is cancelled. If it cannot be created the original pick still works.

features.title: The sort dropdown doesn't work to sort clips by various dates.
features.summary: The backend sorting was already correct (covered by store tests), but the history hook only refetched when the filter or query changed. Choosing a new order updated the setting without reloading the list, so nothing moved. The hook now takes the sort order as a dependency, so every selection of Last used ↑/↓ or Captured ↑/↓ immediately refetches and reorders the history.

features.title: Add the filter function to "collections" and limit of 6
features.summary: Collections now behave like Archives and Tags: a filter box matches names as you type (Enter opens the first match, Escape clears), the list shows the configured sidebar limit (6 by default) and offers Show all with a compact scrollable list. The Sidebar lists setting in Appearance controls the shared limit.

features.title: In color preview thumbnail view and properties, show both the HEX and RGB values
features.summary: Colour swatches now render the normalised HEX code and the matching rgb(r, g, b) value together, in the list thumbnail, the grid card and the preview pane. The Details section already listed both and still does; the swatch tooltip repeats them so the values remain available when a tiny thumbnail truncates the second line.

features.title: for the GIF utility add a button to add your custom gif file
features.summary: The GIF utility toolbar has an Add GIF file button that opens a .gif picker. The chosen file is sniffed for the GIF header, capped at 32 MB and copied into the media folder under a content-addressed name, so the shelf entry survives the original being moved or deleted. It appears immediately in Your GIFs and copies through CF_HDROP, preserving every frame. Imported entries are validated when settings load: only bare .gif names inside the media folder are accepted.

features.title: Performance for the Emoji all view is still poor
features.summary: The earlier fixes were present: rows are virtualised and glyphs are pre-rasterised through an idle canvas. The remaining cost came from the virtual window itself and from how the warmer forced rasterisation. Row tops are now precomputed so scrolling finds the window with a binary search instead of two linear scans plus a prefix sum; scroll events are coalesced to one render per animation frame; the renderer keeps one contain: layout paint style per row; and the glyph warmer draws 64 glyphs per readback instead of 4, cutting canvas readbacks for the All view from about 134 to 9 while keeping the same idle-time budget.

features.title: Create Color Scheme from Screenshot
features.summary: Image clips now show a Color scheme box in the preview pane with an Extract button. The backend samples the stored image on a bounded grid, buckets pixels into a coarse RGB cube, averages each bucket and returns up to five dominant colors, rejecting near-duplicate shades. The pane renders them as swatches with hex and RGB values; clicking a swatch copies its hex code. Verified against a red/green/blue/white test image, which produced four swatches, and copying the first swatch put #4169e1 on the clipboard.

features.title: BUG The magnified view when taking color samples is flicking when it's being used.
features.summary: The magnifier was drawing straight to the window surface in several GDI calls, so each tick could show a partially repainted frame and moving the popup forced extra repaints. It now composes the zoom, crosshair, footer chip and label into an off-screen compatible bitmap and blits the finished frame in one operation, and the window is moved with SWP_NOREDRAW so Windows cannot paint between the move and the blit. The result is a stable preview with no flicker while the cursor moves.

features.title: Add a clear filters button to gif search box when not empty

features.title: Drag files, text or images into the copy list window to create new entries
features.summary: Files dragged from Explorer onto the window now become history entries. A drop overlay appears while the drag is over the window; on release the backend decodes a single image file, a single small UTF-8 text file, or otherwise records one file-list clip of every path. Dropped entries use the same preview, search and hash rules as clipboard captures, so they dedupe against existing clips. Text and images dragged from other applications cannot carry a path through Windows' native drop channel, so they are not imported; copy them instead.

features.title: Copying a GIF still doesn't retain it's animation.
features.summary: The recovered animation was already being stored and copied correctly, but the app kept showing the rasterised still frame. The media scheme serves `.gif` files as image/gif, so the animation plays inside CopyPaste as well as on paste.

features.title: Make the options screen pop out into it's own window

The gear in the title bar and the tray's Settings item both open (or focus) a single `settings` window that loads the same bundle with `?route=settings`; Escape closes it. The overlay window stays a pure history surface, and the new window is covered by the existing capability set.

features.title: When sampling colors on the screen, allow no interactions of elements on the screen

The picking loop pumps its own message queue so the hook actually runs, and the hook is removed as soon as the pick finishes, times out or is cancelled.

features.title: Export clip to Markdown
features.summary:
Quick capture into a Markdown vault (Obsidian or any PKM): export a text clip as a .md note, one click once a folder is set.

Behaviour
• Actions: context menu, detail pane, bulk bar, and Ctrl+Shift+M (writes, reports the folder, then hides the overlay).
• Filename: "YYYY-MM-DD <first line>" — leading Markdown markers stripped, illegal and reserved Windows names handled, unique_path for repeats.
• Body copied as-is with CRLF normalised to LF. No auto headings or rewriting.
• YAML front matter (default on): created, source, tags, clip id — every value quoted and escaped.
• Bulk export writes one .md per text clip; image and file clips are skipped and counted in the notice.

Settings
• markdownExportDir — empty asks each time, otherwise one-click.
• markdownFrontMatter — default on.
• markdownDatePrefix — default on.

Rules
• A configured folder must already exist: no create_dir_all, so a moved vault errors instead of silently reappearing.
• High-confidence secret clips ask before being written to disk.
• Clearing the folder restores "ask each time".

Tests: Markdown render/CRLF/YAML escaping, filename reserved names and collisions, settings sanitiser, store skips non-text clips.

features.title: Colour scheme: perceptual extraction and auto-generation
features.summary:
Make the colour scheme panel produce a usable palette without a click.

Extraction
• Cluster in OKLab instead of raw RGB, so "close" means perceptually close.
• Cap low-chroma (neutral) entries at 2 slots so a screenshot's white and greys cannot crowd out the accents; always keep at least one chromatic entry when the image has one.
• Keep the result deterministic (frequency order, stable tie-break) so tests stay meaningful.

Auto-generation
• Generate the scheme on first view of an image clip: no Extract click, computed off the UI thread.
• Persist it per clip (own table, so list queries stay unaffected) and serve the stored copy afterwards.
• Drop the Refresh button: extraction is deterministic, so re-running produced identical colours.

features.title: Tag images that contain a face (YuNet via tract, pure Rust)
features.summary: Tag image clips that contain a face so they can be filtered as People, listed under Images in the sidebar beside Screenshots. Engine: tract 0.23 (pure Rust, Apache-2.0/MIT) running the MIT YuNet detector from OpenCV Zoo, model vendored at src-tauri/assets (227 KB, weights compiled in). Measured: ~90 ms one-off model parse and compile, 85-100 ms per 640x640 pass, on the existing background worker beside OCR. Store gains face_count/face_state (schema v8) filled by run_faces, which letterboxes to 640x640 (BGR, 0-255, right/bottom zero padding), decodes the cls/obj/bbox heads at strides 8/16/32, takes the geometric-mean score and applies IoU-0.3 NMS. Images > People filters face_count > 0 and the preview pane reports the count. Capture > Detect faces is a local toggle (default on); detections fail soft and existing images are backfilled at startup. Verified on a real portrait: 1 face at 0.937 confidence.

features.title: Scrolling screenshot mode
features.summary: Implemented in 0.13.16, awaiting a real-window check. A fourth capture button picks a window, brings it forward, parks the pointer in it and sends wheel bursts a page at a time. After each scroll the next frame is captured and stitch::overlap_rows finds how many of its top rows already exist at the bottom of what has been stitched (48-row template, sampled channels, hundredths-of-a-level scoring, ties broken towards the larger overlap); only the new rows are appended. Stops on a window resize, an unmatched frame, no new rows, 20 scroll steps or 20,000 px, and keeps the partial result. Five stitching unit tests cover a scrolled page, a still page, unrelated frames, a small scroll and short buffers. Rendering quirks (sticky headers, lazy-loaded images, inertial scrolling) can leave a seam, so this needs trying against a real browser window.
